claims.description: Configured CSS text and document style elements contribute rules in cascade order.

notes.text: Inline and stylesheet declarations share Lightning CSS parsing and origin/importance ordering. declaration-cascade verifies font-relative declaration order, cross-source importance, and custom-property priority.
Configured stylesheet text and document `style` elements are combined with other supported stylesheet sources in cascade order.

Parsed source trees and collected rules are cached per attachment and source revision. Changing one sheet preserves other parsed sheets. Selector candidate indexes and matching results are scoped to each layout computation, while pure declaration/selector string caches have bounded capacity.

claims.description: A configurable deterministic user-agent presentation layer cascades below author styles.

notes.text: The portable profile supplies declarations to the common cascade; none omits its presentation defaults. HTML sizing hints rank above normal user-agent rules and below normal author rules. Important user-agent rules outrank important author rules. Native-control intrinsic metrics and HTML non-rendering constraints remain separate.

claims.description: Accessible linked stylesheets contribute readable CSS rules.

notes.text: Cross-origin or otherwise inaccessible linked stylesheets cannot contribute rules and route through the unsupported CSS policy.

claims.description: `document.adoptedStyleSheets` participate in their configured cascade order.
Viewport media rules select stylesheet branches from the configured layout viewport.
conditions: Supported media types are `screen` and `all`; other media types do not match.
Width, height, orientation, and aspect-ratio features use the configured viewport.
Query lists, `not`, `only`, `and`, and nested media rules are supported.

notes.text: Wide landscape and narrow portrait fixtures verify matching and non-matching responsive branches against Chromium.
Viewport changes reuse parsed stylesheet source trees and re-evaluate media conditions. Inactive branches retain lazy unsupported-CSS policy routing.

claims.description: Stylesheet at-rules other than supported viewport media rules are not part of the source subset.

notes.text: Unsupported media features and other at-rules route through the configured unsupported CSS policy. Parser recovery reports the authored stylesheet when rules are discarded; strict policy and callback errors propagate unchanged. Unsupported rule values retain authored stylesheet text rather than AST JSON. Unsupported declaration diagnostics preserve authored CSS values when the typed value stringifier has no CSS representation.
